review_scope.sampling_note: Reviewed the existing 1 FPS sampled packet frames, not every source frame. Action intervals are bounded by sampled observations and are approximate; do not interpret the bounds as frame-exact event times.

episode_summary: A person handles a Canon DSLR with a zoom lens on a tabletop. Within the reviewed interval, the lens is removed from the camera body and later reattached; the front lens cap is then removed and replaced. These are two different part-removal events, not a replay or a repeated removal of the same component.

events.action: detaches the zoom lens assembly from the camera body

evidence.observation: Lens appears mounted on the camera body; the person is holding and turning the assembly.
The camera body is visibly separated from the zoom lens, which is held in the other hand.

events.action: reattaches the zoom lens assembly to the camera body

evidence.observation: The lens is positioned over the camera mount; the exact point of engagement is not clear in this sampled frame.
The lens is visibly mounted on the camera body.

events.confidence: medium; sampled frame at the start bound is partially occluded

events.action: removes the front cap from the still-mounted zoom lens

evidence.observation: The hand is manipulating the front of the mounted lens; the cap appears to be in the process of removal.
The exposed lens front and detached cap held separately are visible.

events.action: replaces the front cap on the mounted zoom lens

evidence.observation: The cap is being brought back to the lens front; exact engagement is obscured by the hand.
The cap is visibly seated on the lens front.

protected_facts: E1 and E3 are two different events involving different components.
Reattaching the lens (E2) and replacing the cap (E4) are not additional removal events.
At the final reviewed checkpoint, the zoom lens is attached to the camera and its front cap is in place.
The video does not establish the camera's power state or whether a photograph was taken.

quality_control.note: This is a pilot annotation by one reviewer using existing sampled frames. It is not ground truth yet. A second annotator should independently mark event intervals, object identity, and state checkpoints from the source video before scoring models. Because prior model experiments exist on this source, use it as a schema pilot or training/development item, not a held-out test example.
